setup: Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat
Hands lightly by your head or across your chest
Lower back resting on the floor
execution: Breathe out and curl your ribs toward your hips
Lift until your shoulder blades leave the floor
faults: Don't pull on your head or neck
Don't sit all the way up from the hips
Don't rush or bounce off the floor

notes: Hands support the head only; the abs do the lifting. If your neck tires first, cross your arms on your chest instead.
To add load, hold a plate on your chest and log it as added weight.
Coaching sources differ on how much crunching is wise. A common middle ground is moderate volume, built up gradually.
If pain lingers or comes back, stop this exercise and get it checked by a physio or doctor.
stopIf: Pain that changes how you move

regressions.name: Crunch with hands sliding up the thighs
regressions.reason: Reaching along the thighs shortens the lever and guides the curl.

progressions.name: Decline crunch
progressions.reason: Longer range against gravity; progress by bench angle.

progressions.name: Weighted crunch
progressions.reason: A plate held on the chest; log it as added weight.

progressions.name: Ab crunch machine
progressions.reason: Adds load in clean stack steps.

substitutions.name: Cable crunch
substitutions.reason: Same curl with stack loading, kneeling at a cable column.

substitutions.name: Reverse crunch
substitutions.reason: Curls from the pelvis up instead of the ribs down.

substitutions.name: Dead bug
substitutions.reason: No spine curling; trains bracing instead.

substitutions.name: Plank
substitutions.reason: Holds the trunk still instead of curling it.

guideBrief.cameraNote: Side view at floor level, figure lying along the frame with the head on the left. A thin mat line under the body.

keyPositions.label: Down
keyPositions.describe: Lying on the back, knees bent about 90°, feet flat. Hands lightly by the head, elbows out. Head, shoulders and lower back on the mat.

keyPositions.label: Curled
keyPositions.describe: Head, shoulders and shoulder blades curled off the mat, ribs drawn toward the hips. Lower back, hips and feet still on the mat. Chin slightly tucked; hands not pulling.

ikHints: Feet, hips and lower back stay on the mat in every frame
emphasise: Only the upper back lifts; the lower back stays down
